messages:
Maya: Quick sync — we need to settle VPC topology tradeoffs for the private deploy launch. Two major asks from field: IP preservation (customers want stable IPs across upgrades) and customer-managed egress control/BYO-NAT. Can we enumerate constraints and a viable rollout plan?
Sam: For upgrades preserving node IPs is tough if we replace instances. We could support floating IPs or elastic network interfaces as a compatibility layer. Elastic NICs add some infra complexity but minimal customer config.
Priya: Floating IPs are fine but customers with strict IP whitelisting want a no-change guarantee. We should distinguish between a best-effort policy and an SLO-backed guarantee.
Alex: On BYO-NAT, customers expect full control over egress for compliance. We can document a supported pattern: route traffic through customer-managed NAT gateway + iptables rules on host. Need to decide if we validate network during install.
Jon: From SRE side, any solution that relies on customer infra increases troubleshooting surface. Suggest we provide a default managed egress mode and an opt-in BYO mode for enterprise. Default should allow simple installs and fallbacks.
Maya: Good. So three axes: 1) IP stability (floating vs ephemeral), 2) egress mode (managed vs BYO), 3) upgrade strategy (in-place vs replace). We need launch criteria for each.
Sam: Propose minimal launch: support managed egress + floating IPs on upgrade window; BYO-NAT as beta that requires network-owner signoff. That reduces blast radius for GA.
Priya: Agree on gating: BYO-NAT requires a preflight network check and a documented rollback path. Preflight could be a simple connectivity test: `curl -I https://controlplane.redwood.local` from a node, plus IP routing sanity check.
Alex: Also surface a delegated DNS option — some customers want internal names to remain stable. We can provide a small agent that updates Route53/CloudDNS records during upgrade if allowed. Keep as opt-in.
Jon: For automation: add a canary rollout flag `--allow-ip-migration=false` in installer and a staged upgrade plan: canary group (5%), monitor for 15m, then full. Deploy-bot: canary deploy initiated by Maya at 2325003000 — status: in_progress 
Maya: Launch criteria draft: (a) Managed egress + floating IP upgrade path tested across two cloud providers; (b) BYO-NAT preflight + rollback documented and tested in at least one customer pilot; (c) Installer exposes explicit flags for egress and IP migration; (d) Healthcheck and canary tooling integrated into console.
Sam: Next steps: engineering spike to prototype floating NIC and DNS agent (1 sprint), Priya to write preflight checklist, Alex to pair with solutions for pilot customers.
Priya: I'll draft the preflight checklist and add required network diagrams.
Alex: I'll reach out to two pilot customers this week.
Maya: Thanks — I'll update the roadmap ticket with these gating criteria and schedule a 30-min sync after the spike. :thumbsup:
